scenario_1_dev.prompt: Developer is on holiday. Need urgent feature: Implement JWT refresh token rotation with Redis blacklist for the auth service.

jira_issue.summary: Implement JWT refresh token rotation with Redis blacklist
jira_issue.description: As an API client, I need secure JWT refresh token rotation with a Redis-backed token blacklist to prevent replay attacks.

exa_grounding.title: OAuth 2.0 and JWT Refresh Token Best Practices 2026
exa_grounding.summary: Refresh token rotation issues a new refresh token every time the current refresh token is exchanged. Revoked or previously used tokens must be invalidated via a Redis blacklist with TTL matching the token lifetime.

exa_grounding.title: Redis-py Async Connection Pooling and Expiring Keys
exa_grounding.summary: Use redis.asyncio.ConnectionPool with retry_on_timeout=True and health_check_interval=30. Store blacklisted JTI hashes using SETEX with matching TTL.

code_files.content:
import pytest
from auth.token_service import TokenService

def test_token_pair_generation():
    service = TokenService()
    tokens = service.generate_token_pair("user_123")
    assert "access_token" in tokens
    assert "refresh_token" in tokens
    assert tokens["user_id"] == "user_123"

def test_refresh_token_rotation():
    service = TokenService()
    tokens1 = service.generate_token_pair("user_123")
    old_refresh = tokens1["refresh_token"]
    tokens2 = service.rotate_refresh_token(old_refresh, "user_123")
    assert tokens2["refresh_token"] != old_refresh
    assert service.is_token_blacklisted(old_refresh) is True

def test_replay_attack_prevention():
    service = TokenService()
    tokens = service.generate_token_pair("user_123")
    old_refresh = tokens["refresh_token"]
    service.rotate_refresh_token(old_refresh, "user_123")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Token has been revoked"):
        service.rotate_refresh_token(old_refresh, "user_123")

scenario_2_pm.prompt: We are launching our Q4 Enterprise SSO and Multi-Tenant RBAC initiative. Please break this down into an Epic with technical user stories, acceptance criteria, story point estimates, and set up our Sprint backlog in Jira.

epic.description: Establish enterprise identity federation (SAML 2.0 / OIDC) and tenant-isolated Role-Based Access Control to support enterprise customers in Q4.

stories.summary: SAML 2.0 and OIDC Identity Provider Federation
acceptance_criteria: Given an enterprise customer with Okta or Azure AD, when they configure SSO, then users can authenticate via SAML 2.0 / OIDC.
Given an expired SAML assertion, when user initiates session, then prompt for re-authentication.

stories.summary: Tenant Isolation Middleware and Schema Partitioning
acceptance_criteria: Given a multi-tenant database, when an API request executes, then all SQL queries are scoped by tenant_id.
Given a cross-tenant data query attempt, when executed, then throw 403 Forbidden.
Given a user role (Admin, Member, Viewer), when accessing resource endpoints, then verify against permission bitmask.
Given custom roles, when created by tenant admin, then support dynamic permission assignment.

stories.summary: Tenant Audit Logging and Compliance Export
acceptance_criteria: Given security-sensitive operations (role change, user invite), when performed, then append immutable event to audit log.
Given a compliance request, when admin clicks export, then download signed JSONL audit report.
